result.summary: Reviewed git diff main...HEAD (16 files) against the four gate questions. (1) Idiomatic vs crutch: json_schema.ex is genuinely idiomatic, not a crutch -- one clear recursive entry point (collect/3) dispatching to small private per-keyword functions (enum_violations/numeric_violations/string_violations/object_violations/array_violations), each returning a list and combined via ++, no nested case-statement pile. Directly compared against lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex (REQ-028): same established style (private per-check functions, Enum.flat_map/++ accumulation, plain non-persisted struct for violations -- ValidationFailure mirrors graph.ex's Violation). The one divergence (type-mismatch short-circuits sibling keyword checks at the same recursion level) is explicitly documented as a deliberate, faithful port of R-Co's own cascade-avoidance behavior, not an inconsistency. registry.ex, event_type.ex, validation_failure.ex all match this codebase's established context-module/same-named-schema-submodule convention (Letflow.Identity/Tenant precedent), binary_id PK, plain attrs :: map() changeset input. (2) Supervision: confirmed zero diff to lib/letflow/process_instance.ex, lib/letflow/instance_supervisor.ex, lib/letflow/application.ex (git diff main...HEAD --stat on all three returns empty). (3) Type-safety gaps: none severe. Validating arbitrary untrusted JSON Schema/payload data is inherently dynamic-data validation -- a stricter static type system wouldn't meaningfully help at the validator's core. Non-blocking note: Registry.resolve_schema_name/1 duplicates (rather than reuses) the exact Repo.get_by(Registration, tenant_id: tenant_id) lookup already present twice in tenant_provisioning.ex (replay_migrations/2 line 161, re_select_registration/1 line 234) -- the module's own comment already flags this and explicitly defers the extraction call to REVIEWER. Judgment: acceptable as-is: extracting now would mean expanding a merged sibling requirement's (REQ-022's) public API beyond the one anticipated touch point (tenant_scoped_migrations/0), for a second call site. Worth watching under a rule-of-three -- if a third module needs the same tenant_id->schema_name resolution, extract a shared Letflow.TenantProvisioning function then. (4) Scope creep: none. Diff's 16 changed files match the handoff's artifacts_in plus process/doc files (requirements.yaml, status history, handoff jsons, orchestrator.log, registry.json, the design doc) -- no other lib/ or priv/ files touched. All 5 of REQ-024's acceptance_criteria are covered: migration applies schema-per-tenant per REQ-022's guard pattern (AC1), register_type/2 returns {:error, :duplicate_event_type_version} on (name, schema_version) collision via pre-check + unique-index backstop (AC2), validate_payload/3 (arity change from /2 to /3 explicitly documented and justified in the moduledoc, not silent) returns field_path (JSON Pointer)/constraint detail on failure (AC3), get_type/2 returns {:error, :unknown_event_type} not nil/exception for an unregistered name (AC4), moduledoc explicitly names the JSON Schema library choice as a decision made at CODE-DESIGNER design time with reasoning, matching AC5's 'explicit open question, not silent' framing. tenant_provisioning.ex's diff is the minimal 2-line array-literal addition to tenant_scoped_migrations/0 plus a moduledoc comment update -- exactly the extension point REQ-022's own design doc and that function's moduledoc named for future tenant-scoped migrations, not unauthorized editing of REQ-022's logic. mix.exs/mix.lock are untouched, confirming the 'no ex_json_schema dependency added' claim is real. REQ-023 (event-store proper, status: pending) is untouched -- this diff doesn't step on it. (5) docs/anti-patterns.md: two existing entries (no local toolchain workaround; don't overwrite requirement_status.yaml), neither applicable to this diff; nothing new to add. (6) Decision 0003 consistency: event_type_registry is explicitly classified under Decision C as a 'regular CRUD table' (grouped with process_definitions, sampled from 004_definitions.sql/002_event_type_registry.sql) rather than an event-log table -- correctly uses a plain binary_id PK, not the (event_id, created_at) composite PK or idempotency-sidecar treatment Decision C reserves for events/events_archive. Migration's guard pattern (if prefix() do ... end, no-op on a plain mix ecto.migrate) matches req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md section 4's required pattern. tenant_id -> Registration -> schema_name resolution verified directly against tenant_provisioning.ex source (not just the claim in registry.ex's own comment) -- both replay_migrations/2 and re_select_registration/1 call the identical Repo.get_by(Registration, tenant_id: tenant_id), confirming Registry.resolve_schema_name/1 genuinely matches the established convention rather than only asserting it does.

issues.description: Registry.resolve_schema_name/1 (lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex) duplicates the tenant_id->Registration->schema_name Repo.get_by lookup already present twice in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex rather than calling a shared function. Already self-flagged in registry.ex's own comment as deferred to REVIEWER. Not blocking for REQ-024 (extraction now would expand REQ-022's already-merged public surface for a single second call site) -- revisit under a rule-of-three if a third module needs the same resolution.
